title: Check S-Tunnel Active Connections and TLS Status
summary: Use the S-Tunnel / Chat path display on the remotely accessed WCS primary computer to inspect the connection list, active connection count, service names, traffic counters, and TLS status.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when verifying whether the live S-Tunnel / Chat path on the WCS primary computer has the expected service connections and successful TLS session status.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a recovery or restart procedure; the source provides connection and TLS inspection only.
Do not treat an isolated "No peer certificate received" message as a recovery instruction. Escalate for interpretation when it conflicts with the overall S-Tunnel / Chat path status.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Remotely access the WCS primary computer and inspect the live S-Tunnel / Chat path connection view and log.
Interpret or escalate inconsistent connection counts, missing services, or TLS status when L2 support cannot determine the condition.

safety_notes: This is an inspection-only diagnostic. Do not restart S-Tunnel or other services based solely on this procedure.
Do not infer recovery from an isolated "No peer certificate received" message.
access_or_tools_needed: Remote access to the WCS primary computer

access_required: L2 or L3 support access to the WCS primary computer
Access to the S-Tunnel / Chat path display
system_preconditions: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application is available on the WCS primary computer.

visual_references.description: S-Tunnel / Chat path display showing the File menu, connections view, active connection messages, service names, traffic counters, and TLS log status.

steps.title: Open the S-Tunnel / Chat path on the WCS primary computer
steps.purpose: Open the live S-Tunnel / Chat path display so its connection log and connection controls can be inspected.
steps.instruction: Using remote access to the WCS primary computer, open the S-Tunnel / Chat path application.
steps.expected_result: The S-Tunnel / Chat path window is visible with its connection log and menu bar.
steps.healthy_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application opens and its log area is available for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application cannot be opened or its connection log is unavailable.

actions.label: Open S-Tunnel
actions.exact_action: Open the S-Tunnel / Chat path application on the WCS primary computer.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the S-Tunnel / Chat path application cannot be opened or the connection log is unavailable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The captured S-Tunnel screen is accessed on the computer and shows the S-Tunnel connection log and menu bar.

steps.title: Open the S-Tunnel connections view
steps.purpose: Navigate to the live connection list used to inspect active S-Tunnel / Chat path services.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel / Chat path application, open the File menu and select the connections option.
steps.expected_result: The S-Tunnel connections view opens and displays the active connection information.
steps.healthy_condition: The connections view is visible and contains connection entries or active-connection status information.
steps.failure_condition: The File menu does not provide the connections option, or the connections view does not open.

actions.label: Open connections
actions.exact_action: Under the S-Tunnel application's File menu, click connections.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the connections option is unavailable or the connections view cannot be opened.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel display instructs the user to click connections under File.

steps.title: Inspect the active service connection list
steps.purpose: Verify that the expected S-Tunnel / Chat path services are represented in the live connection list.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel connections view, inspect the active connection list for the expected service connections, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.
steps.expected_result: The active connection list shows the expected service entries, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The expected service connections are present in the active connection list.
steps.failure_condition: An expected service connection is missing from the active connection list.

actions.label: Inspect service entries
actions.exact_action: Check the active connection list for AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if an expected service connection is missing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel display states that it should show 3 connections including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat.

steps.title: Verify active connection count and traffic counters
steps.purpose: Confirm the expected number of active S-Tunnel / Chat path connections and verify that the live services show traffic counters.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel connections view and log, confirm that the display reports 3 active connection(s). Review the per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.
steps.expected_result: The display reports 3 active connection(s), and the active service entries show bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.
steps.healthy_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path reports 3 active connection(s) and the service entries contain traffic-counter values.
steps.failure_condition: The active connection count is not 3, or the expected service entries do not show traffic-counter information.

actions.label: Check active count
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the display reports 3 active connection(s).

actions.label: Review traffic counters
actions.exact_action: Review the per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the active connection count is not 3.
Escalate if the expected service entries do not show the traffic counters needed to assess the connection.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel log reports Listed 3 active connection(s) and shows per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket.

steps.title: Verify successful TLS status in the connection log
steps.purpose: Confirm that the active S-Tunnel / Chat path connections have observable successful TLS session status.
steps.instruction: Review the S-Tunnel connection log for messages including "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or a connected status.
steps.expected_result: The connection log contains successful TLS negotiation messages and may also show session reuse, a connected status, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, or authenticated application data.
steps.healthy_condition: The live S-Tunnel log shows "TLS negotiation finished successfully" for the relevant connection and/or a connected status with session reuse.
steps.failure_condition: The connection log does not show successful TLS negotiation or connected-status evidence for an expected active connection.

actions.label: Check TLS messages
actions.exact_action: Check the connection log for "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or a connected status.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the connection log does not show successful TLS negotiation.
Do not treat an isolated "No peer certificate received" message as a recovery instruction; escalate for interpretation if it conflicts with the overall connection status.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel log contains successful TLS negotiation, session reuse, connected status, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, authenticated application data, and a No peer certificate received message.

success_criteria: The S-Tunnel / Chat path connections view is open on the WCS primary computer.
The expected service connections, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed, are present.
Per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters are visible.
The connection log shows "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or connected status.
healthy_conditions: The S-Tunnel / Chat path reports 3 active connection(s).
Expected service names are present in the active connection list.
Active services show traffic counters for bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket.
The connection log shows successful TLS negotiation and observable connected or session-reuse status.
failure_conditions: The active connection count is not 3.
An expected service connection is missing.
Traffic counters are absent for an expected active service.
The connection log lacks successful TLS negotiation or connected-status evidence.
An isolated "No peer certificate received" message conflicts with the overall connection status and requires interpretation.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the active connection count is not 3, an expected service connection is missing, or successful TLS negotiation is not shown.
Do not restart S-Tunnel or other services under this diagnostic; the source does not provide a recovery or restart procedure.
Escalate an isolated "No peer certificate received" message for interpretation when it conflicts with the overall connection status.
